paths.description: Public Seller Central landing page, representing the main marketing template and entry to seller onboarding.
Seller sign-in form, representing authentication, form semantics, validation, and recovery.
Start-selling destination reached from registration, representing the onboarding decision and signup landing surface.
Spanish locale variant, representing localization and translated layout.

findings.summary: The public and sign-in surfaces ignore the user’s dark-mode preference.
findings.evidence: The dark-emulated screenshot is pixel-identical to the light capture and the probe reports color-scheme: normal with no prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() CSS.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and preference-driven surface, text, border, and image treatments using prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Navigation and state changes have no transition treatment.
findings.evidence: The live CSS probe found no view-transition declarations; the covered route changes and sign-in validation swap state without a View Transition.
findings.suggestedFix: Use same-document View Transitions for meaningful state changes and cross-document transitions for eligible marketing navigation, while respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: Long-page navigation does not respond to scroll state.
findings.evidence: The landing page is over 4,200 CSS px tall, but the CSS probe found no scroll-state query, scroll timeline, or progress treatment for navigation chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Use scroll-state container queries or a lightweight progress affordance so navigation responds to long-page position.

findings.summary: The pages omit the viewport meta tag and render a desktop-sized CSS viewport on phones.
findings.evidence: At a requested 360x800 viewport, layout reports innerWidth 1000 on home and 980 on sign-in, hasViewportMeta false, and Chrome scales the desktop layout to about 0.36, shrinking text and controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"> and retest layouts at true mobile CSS widths with intrinsic/fluid sizing.

findings.summary: Several controls and links fall below comfortable touch-target dimensions.
findings.evidence: The live probe found visible links only 14–21 CSS px high, and Lighthouse sign-in reports seven target-size failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Give interactive targets at least a 24x24 CSS px area, preferably 44x44 for primary touch actions, with sufficient spacing and visible focus.

findings.summary: The public landing page loads too slowly for the primary path.
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 9.2 s, FCP 4.3 s, Speed Index 7.4 s, and TTI 14.5 s; the independent trace measured LCP 3.27 s and FCP 3.25 s with low TBT, confirming network/LCP rather than sustained main-thread blocking as the main problem.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP image and critical CSS, reduce the font and image waterfall, and defer nonessential page sections and telemetry.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is delayed by a large render-blocking and font/image waterfall.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 123 requests and 3.36 MB transferred, including five parser-inserted stylesheets and 1.37 MB across 15 fonts; DOM confirmation shows all five active stylesheets, while most scripts are async but three body scripts are synchronous.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline or consolidate critical CSS, defer noncritical styles, subset and reduce fonts, and explicitly prioritize only the LCP asset.

findings.summary: The landing page ships substantial unused CSS and JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 279 KiB unused JavaScript and 136 KiB unused CSS, while the DOM loads duplicate aos.js and assets-Sell.js URLs in both async head and synchronous body contexts.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate script inclusion, split route/component bundles, and load optional marketing and analytics code conditionally.

findings.summary: Image and ARIA semantics are incomplete on primary surfaces.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports 43 homepage images without alt text and seven role/ARIA mismatches; the sign-in audit adds an unnamed link and invalid ARIA value. The image primitive counted 93 img elements without alt, including many decorative icons.
findings.suggestedFix: Add meaningful alt text where images convey content, empty alt for decoration, and correct the invalid role/ARIA pairings and unnamed controls.

findings.summary: The sign-in template lacks a main landmark and the mobile menu trigger is not a semantic control.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports no main landmark on sign-in. On the landing page the hamburger is a span inside a focusable header rather than a named button, even though visible focus itself is present.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the sign-in content in <main> and implement the menu trigger as a named <button> with expanded/controls state and logical focus order.

findings.summary: Mobile reflow and zoom start from the wrong viewport.
findings.evidence: Both representative sellercentral.com templates omit a viewport declaration, causing 980–1000 CSS px layouts to be downscaled into a 360 px device viewport; Lighthouse also reports seven sign-in touch-target failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare the device-width viewport, preserve user scaling, then verify 320 CSS px reflow, 200% zoom, and target spacing.

findings.summary: Asset sizing and platform hygiene have avoidable defects.
findings.evidence: The image primitive reports 99 of 100 images without width/height attributes and 46 oversized images. Lighthouse reports one deprecated API warning.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve image space with width/height or aspect-ratio, serve correctly sized sources, and replace the deprecated API identified in Lighthouse.

findings.summary: Both primary templates are ineligible for the back/forward cache.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports four BFCache failure reasons on the landing page and two on sign-in, increasing repeat-navigation cost.
findings.suggestedFix: Inspect the Lighthouse BFCache reasons, remove unload/cache-control blockers where safe, and verify restoration with pageshow.persisted.

findings.summary: The sign-in archetype has no meta description.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse SEO passes the public homepage title/description but reports that the sign-in document has no meta description.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a concise, unique description for the sign-in page while retaining the descriptive title.

findings.summary: The public organization/commerce landing page has share tags but no structured data.
findings.evidence: The metadata probe found Open Graph and Twitter tags but zero JSON-LD or microdata blocks on a public Amazon Seller Central organization/service page.
findings.suggestedFix: Add accurate Organization and WebSite/Service JSON-LD that matches the visible content and canonical URL.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes are incomplete.
findings.evidence: HTTPS and HSTS are present, but the header probe found no CSP, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. Cookie evidence reports 14 cookies without Secure and auth-like session-id/session-token cookies readable by script and using SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP, explicit Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy, and review cookie scope so sensitive cookies are Secure, HttpOnly, and use the narrowest viable SameSite policy.

findings.summary: The public landing page has a large analytics and third-party footprint before user action.
findings.evidence: The tracker probe records 15 third-party origins; the HAR attributes 118 of 123 requests and 3.21 of 3.36 MB to non-sellercentral origins, including Adobe/Demdex and Everest redirects.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit each third party for necessity, gate nonessential analytics behind user choice where required, minimize identifiers, and batch or remove chatty telemetry.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defenses are only partially configured.
findings.evidence: HSTS and X-Frame-Options are present, but no CSP/frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy was observed; the cookies evidence also shows broad SameSite=None use.
findings.suggestedFix: Add CSP with frame-ancestors, explicit referrer and permissions policies, and narrow cross-site cookie use; consider Trusted Types for the authenticated app.

findings.summary: The public landing page exposes little meaningful content to non-JavaScript clients.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured only 5% raw-to-rendered word coverage and classified the marketing page as a JavaScript shell; the raw HTML has title/description but no H1, while the rendered page has 284 content tokens.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the primary heading, offer, navigation, and key seller guidance, then hydrate enhancements without replacing core content.

findings.summary: Locale metadata is correct, but the stylesheet does not use logical properties.
findings.evidence: The Spanish variant correctly sets lang=es-ES and renders translated content, but the CSS probe found no logical inline/block properties, reducing resilience for RTL/writing-mode expansion.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep the correct locale switching and replace physical spacing/positioning with logical properties before adding RTL locales.

findings.summary: The sign-in template contains an invalid autocomplete configuration.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reports an autocomplete-valid failure on the authentication form, despite this being a high-value sign-in surface.
findings.suggestedFix: Use valid autocomplete tokens such as username and current-password/webauthn on the corresponding fields and preserve password-manager behavior.

findings.summary: The page transfers oversized and weakly constrained media.
findings.evidence: The image audit reports 46 oversized images, seven legacy-format images, five without responsive sources, and 99 without dimensions; images transfer 1.07 MB on the initial load.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve responsive AVIF/WebP sources sized to their slots, reserve dimensions, lazy-load below-fold media, and remove unused duplicate image nodes.

findings.summary: Third-party, font, and media cost is disproportionate for a marketing entry page.
findings.evidence: The 3.36 MB load includes 1.37 MB of fonts, 1.07 MB of images, and 3.21 MB attributed to third-party origins; 15 separate fonts and 118 third-party requests dominate the budget.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a page-weight and third-party budget, subset fonts, reduce families/weights, defer below-fold media, and delay nonessential telemetry.

findings.summary: Nonessential background analytics and duplicate resources create avoidable work.
findings.evidence: The initial load sends analytics requests to Adobe/Demdex, Everest and Amazon telemetry endpoints, while the DOM includes duplicate aos.js and assets-Sell.js loads; this work occurs before a seller chooses an action.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate resource execution, defer nonessential analytics until idle or consent, and batch the telemetry that remains.

findings.summary: The agent-relevant seller onboarding surface exposes no structured capability contract.
findings.evidence: The live probe found no WebMCP or agentic tool registration, and the public content is only 5% present in raw HTML, leaving agents to infer actions from a JS-heavy visual surface.
findings.suggestedFix: For safe onboarding assistance, expose narrowly scoped, user-confirmed WebMCP tools or agentic forms and keep the explanatory content server-readable.
